value_as_stated: Ore Shale traced ~100 km; grey-green passing laterally to black carbonaceous; 5 to >50 m thick
quote_ocr: The Ore Shale is a remarkably persistent horizon that can be traced from Chililabombwe to Luanshya, a distance of approximately 100 km. It is a grey-green, silty argillite, 5 to more than 50 m thick, passing laterally to a black, carbonaceous argillite.
source: Binda, P.L. and Mulgrew, J.R. 1974. Stratigraphy of copper occurrences in the Zambian Copperbelt. In Bartholome (ed.), Gisements stratiformes et provinces cupriferes, Liege.

parameter: ore patch length; gap over basement high
value_as_stated: orebody C ~5 km strike, 400 m barren pyritic gap over basement paleohill
quote_ocr: The lowermost of these orebodies ("C") extends for a strike length of approximately 5 km, with a 400 m wide barren (pyritic) gap over a Basement paleohill.
source: Binda, P.L. and Mulgrew, J.R. 1974. Stratigraphy of copper occurrences in the Zambian Copperbelt. In Bartholome (ed.), Gisements stratiformes et provinces cupriferes, Liege.

value_as_stated: Keweenaw copper province a linear zone ~200 km
quote_ocr: The Lake Superior copper deposits are contained in an area known as the Keweenaw peninsula, a linear zone some 200 km in length along the south shore of Lake Superior
source: Brown, A.C. 1974. The copper province of northern Michigan, U.S.A.. In Bartholome (ed.), Gisements stratiformes et provinces cupriferes, Liege.

value_as_stated: six ore bodies over ~200 km; each ~30 km2
quote_ocr: six copper-shale ore bodies exposed in the Flowerpot Shale and San Angelo Sandstone along a total distance of some 200 km in Oklahoma and Texas. Individual ore bodies range from 15 to 45 cm thick and cover about 30 km?.
source: Johnson, K.S. 1974. Permian copper shales of southwestern United States. In Bartholome (ed.), Gisements stratiformes et provinces cupriferes, Liege.

value_as_stated: deposits over 150 km; each 3-10 km long, 1-4 km wide
quote_ocr: They extend a total of 150 km along the outcrop of Flowerpot and San Angelo strata in Texas (fig. 3). ... Individual deposits are traceable for 3 to 10 km along the outcrop ... and appear to be 1 to 4 km wide (east-west).
source: Johnson, K.S. 1974. Permian copper shales of southwestern United States. In Bartholome (ed.), Gisements stratiformes et provinces cupriferes, Liege.

value_as_stated: ore bodies ~10 km by 3 km, ~30 km2, elongate parallel to Permian shoreline
quote_ocr: Ore deposits are typically about 20 cm thick, are elongated north-south or northeast-southwest (subparallel to the inferred Permian shoreline), have dimensions of about 10 km by 3 km, and cover about 30 km2.
source: Johnson, K.S. 1974. Permian copper shales of southwestern United States. In Bartholome (ed.), Gisements stratiformes et provinces cupriferes, Liege.

quote_ocr: Similar occurrences are present in a narrow belt that extends more than 150 miles to the southwest (G. Harron, personal communication).
source: Kirkham, R.V. 1974. A synopsis of Canadian stratiform copper deposits in sedimentary sequences. In Bartholome (ed.), Gisements stratiformes et provinces cupriferes, Liege.
note: conformable zones in schists; weaker analog

value_as_stated: host sediments in sinuous palaeolittoral zones with reducing conditions, close to underlying unconformities
quote_ocr: The host sediments formed in sinuous palaeolittoral zones and contain evidence of biological activity and associated reducing conditions. ... Generally the copper mineralization occurs in transgressive marine sediments close to underlying unconformities.
source: Rowlands, N.J. 1974. The gitology of some Adelaidean stratiform copper occurrences. In Bartholome (ed.), Gisements stratiformes et provinces cupriferes, Liege.
note: local pre-t0 analog; bridges piece 1 and piece 2

value_as_stated: palaeohighs from block-faulted basement at Copper Claim, Gunson, Yudnamutana; primary rock colours grey, black or green
quote_ocr: Such palaeohighs are interpreted at Copper Claim, Gunson, Yudnamutana. ... Primary rock colours (except Dutchmans) are grey, black or green, suggesting foul bottom euxinic conditions.
source: Rowlands, N.J. 1974. The gitology of some Adelaidean stratiform copper occurrences. In Bartholome (ed.), Gisements stratiformes et provinces cupriferes, Liege.

value_as_stated: basal Nonesuch units persistent ~20 miles east and west of White Pine (>= ~64 km); a marker layer >= 28 miles (~45 km) east-west
quote_ocr: the stratigraphic subdivisions of the lowermost part of the Nonesuch shale are more or less persistent for distances of 20 miles east and west of the White Pine mine. ... The environment favorable for deposition of sediments like those at White Pine therefore existed over an area many times larger than that of the White Pine copper deposit itself.
source: White, W.S. and Wright, J.C. 1954. The White Pine copper deposit, Ontonagon County, Michigan. Economic Geology 49, 675-716.

value_as_stated: ore body under an area of several square miles; 10 square miles drilled
quote_ocr: a multimillion-ton body of low-grade ore underlying an area of several square miles
source: White, W.S. and Wright, J.C. 1954. The White Pine copper deposit, Ontonagon County, Michigan. Economic Geology 49, 675-716.
note: side of a square for 3 to 5 sq mi = 2.8 to 3.6 km (translation, 'several' read as 3 to 5)

value_as_stated: ~600 ft grey siltstone (Nonesuch) over 2,300-5,500 ft red sandstones and conglomerates
quote_ocr: The Nonesuch shale, of late Keweenawan age, is about 600 feet thick and is composed largely of gray siltstone. It overlies 2,300 to 5,500 feet of red sandstones and conglomerates
source: White, W.S. and Wright, J.C. 1954. The White Pine copper deposit, Ontonagon County, Michigan. Economic Geology 49, 675-716.
note: OCR of '5,500' read from the text layer as '$,$00'

value_as_stated: Cu-Fe fringe a single blanket surface 20 to 50 ft (6 to 15 m) above the Nonesuch base; barren pyritic shale above
quote_ocr: This narrow fringe forms a blanket-like surface which cross-cuts bedding at shallow angles. ... the actual upper limit of copper mineralization in the White Pine area occurs at various stratigraphic levels 20 to 50 feet above the base of the Nonesuch.
source: Brown, A.C. 1971. Zoning in the White Pine copper deposit, Ontonagon County, Michigan. Economic Geology 66, 543-573.
